contract: #156/#225 current-apps parity: the switcher's Rose row (Launcher3) and Rose's apps (Home) show the SAME set, or the same explicit cannot-confirm state.

categories.cards: a complete, same-user list: exactly these packages are shown, nothing else
categories.genuine_empty: attested complete and empty: 'not using any apps'
categories.cannot_confirm: incomplete, unavailable, locked, malformed or not yet reported: no app cards at all, an explicit status, never genuine_empty

scope: Membership scope is every live ComputerControl session device that the controller owns for the current user. The controller runs at most one session (it closes the old one before starting another), so Home's single controller reply and Launcher3's per-device snapshot describe the same scope. If Launcher3 ever sees more than one live controller-owned device, or any of them incomplete, the whole row is cannot_confirm. Launcher3 also treats any device that is incomplete, or arrays that do not line up, as cannot_confirm; 'loading' (no snapshot or reply yet) is shown without cards and counts as cannot_confirm.

inputs.platform: the per-device view both sources come from: devices[{owner: controller|other, complete, apps}] (PR361 listener / getAutomatedApps). null: no paired platform state (controller-only case).
inputs.controllerReply: the phone-local call("current_apps") reply App Core derives from it (PR364 shape). null: a case only Launcher3 can see.
inputs.controllerInputs: optional: the controller state App Core's test (os/background-control/tests/test_current_apps_parity.py) runs through the production controller CurrentApps; the reply it produces must match controllerReply's status, sessionStatus, complete, incompleteReason, source and apps (packageName/front/target, in order). sessionId, taskId and generation are illustrative.

cases.name: no_session
cases.note: source is session_windows: with no live session the controller does not read the platform (App Core correction of Home's draft value; source never changes the category).

cases.name: none_without_attestation
cases.note: an empty list that is not attested complete is never genuine_empty

cases.name: two_live_controller_devices
cases.note: Launcher3 only: the controller reports its one session, so Home never sees this; the row fails closed rather than union two devices.

cases.name: session_unreleased_cleanup_failed
cases.note: App Core: the controller still holds a session whose close failed (cleanup_failed); its device may still run apps, so this is never genuine_empty. platform is null: Launcher3 cannot see that the session is unreleased (see residualDifferences).

cases.name: target_finished_other_app_remains
cases.note: A finished target removes it; the app still on the session device stays (membership is the platform's, never the session target).

cases.name: malformed_platform_answer
cases.note: The platform answer itself is malformed (here the userId has the wrong type): Launcher3 rejects the snapshot; the controller falls back to its session windows, marked incomplete.

owner: App Core owns this common transport parity fixture (#156/#225). Home owns its reader/render tests, OS Product its Launcher3 tests; both read this file and do not edit it. Add cases through App Core.

knownGaps.name: lingering_unreleased_device
knownGaps.description: A close failed (controller cleanup_failed) and the old device still runs apps. Launcher3 sees one complete controller-owned device and shows its apps; the controller knows the session is unreleased but cannot read the old device's apps through its session view, so Home shows cannot_confirm. Genuinely controlled apps must not be hidden, so neither side may switch to empty.
knownGaps.closesWith: OS Core owner-scoped device view: the controller reads the same per-device snapshot Launcher3 gets, for the devices it owns (see ownerDeviceViewContract).

knownGaps.name: replacement_old_and_new_devices
knownGaps.description: The old session closed and a new one started while the old device's activities are still finishing. Launcher3 sees two controller-owned devices and shows cannot_confirm; the controller's session view sees only the new device and Home shows its apps.
knownGaps.closesWith: OS Core owner-scoped device view: the controller reads the same per-device snapshot Launcher3 gets, for the devices it owns (see ownerDeviceViewContract).

ownerDeviceViewContract.status: proposed to OS Core; not implemented; no framework edit until agreed
ownerDeviceViewContract.method: public android.os.Bundle getOwnedAutomatedDevices() on the existing extensions entry the controller already uses (com.android.extensions.computercontrol.ComputerControlExtensions), reflective like the rest; it needs no session object, so it also answers after a failed close or between sessions
ownerDeviceViewContract.caller: Binder.getCallingUid(): only devices whose recorded owner uid equals the caller's uid are returned; never another owner's device, package or count; no permission, role or exemption
ownerDeviceViewContract.user: the caller's own user only (UserHandle.getUserId(callingUid)); another user's activity on a listed device is omitted and that device's deviceComplete is false

keys.generation: long: the SAME global generation as the AutomatedPackageListener onAutomatedDevicesChanged/onAutomatedDeviceAppsChanged snapshot that contains this content
keys.deviceIds: int[]: every caller-owned ComputerControl session device that currently runs apps (the listener's rule)
keys.appPackageNames: String[] parallel to appDeviceIds: non-finishing activities of the owner's user, front or hidden

ownerDeviceViewContract.atomicity: read under the AutomatedPackagesRepository lock as one snapshot, identical to what the listener dispatches for that generation
ownerDeviceViewContract.lifecycle: a device appears when it runs apps and leaves when its apps finish or it closes, exactly as in the listener; a lingering device after a failed close stays listed; no history
ownerDeviceViewContract.errors: IllegalStateException when unavailable (the controller then keeps today's fail-closed fallback)
ownerDeviceViewContract.consumerRule: both surfaces then apply one rule to the same snapshot: no device -> genuine_empty; exactly one complete device -> its apps (cards, or genuine_empty when none); more than one device or any incomplete -> cannot_confirm
ownerDeviceViewContract.scope: exactly the subset of Launcher3's listener snapshot whose devices the caller owns: same repository, same generation, same per-device apps and completeness, including a device still being torn down or left by a failed close, until the repository drops it (its apps finish or onDeviceClosed); Launcher3 filters its snapshot to owner package dev.pixel.backgroundcontrol with the controller's uid, the controller receives only its own devices, so both evaluate the same device set

alternativesConsidered.retainedSessionGetAutomatedApps: Does not close either gap. lingering_unreleased_device: PR361 ComputerControlSessionImpl.close sets the sticky mAutomatedAppsClosed before the device is torn down, so after a failed close the retained session answers closed with no apps while Launcher3 still lists the device; Home would show genuine_empty and hide controlled apps. replacement_old_and_new_devices: after a successful close the controller holds no binder for the old device at all.
alternativesConsidered.releasingSignal: Could make lingering_unreleased_device fail closed on both sides (Launcher3 marks a releasing device cannot_confirm), but not replacement_old_and_new_devices, where the controller has no view of the old device; it also needs a new per-device state in the listener.
